member.name: T:Fuse.IO.Ply.FieldBufferLifecycle
member.summary:
When the PLY field buffers of a in GpuOnly mode are on the GPU, when the consumer has to (re)initialise from them, and when they may be released. Kept apart from the loader so the rules can be checked without a graphics device.
Every frame the caller passes the release switch, the init request (in the Gallery A forest: preheating) and the time. The answer says whether the consumer should read the fields now () and whether the loader has to release or reload them.
- Init pending: set by a new file load and by the rising edge of the init request. While it is set, the consumer reads the fields as soon as they are on the GPU (also outside a preheat). It is cleared only after the fields were read for and the init request is off. So a load that finishes after the preheat, or a preheat shorter than a reload, still initialises once the data is there. - InitFields = fields on the GPU AND (init request OR init pending). Never true without the fields. - Release: only with the switch on, no init request, nothing pending, and after one completed init since the file was loaded. - Reload: when released and the fields are needed (switch off, init request, or init pending). A failed reload is tried again after .

member.name: P:Fuse.IO.Ply.PlyOctreeLoader.InitFields
member.summary: True while the consumer should read the fields: they are on the GPU AND (init request OR an init is pending). An init is pending after every file load and after every rising edge of the init request, until the fields were read for 2 s with no request. So a load that ends after the preheat, or a preheat shorter than a reload, still initialises once. Never true without the fields.

member.name: M:Fuse.IO.Ply.PlyOctreeLoader.StreamFieldsFromCache(Fuse.IO.Ply.PlyOctreeLoader.PlyReloadSource,Stride.Graphics.GraphicsDevice,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: The reload's normal path: the fields come straight from the PLY disk cache entry, one by one through one unmanaged buffer of the largest field (0.75 GiB for the forest), each uploaded before the next is read. Null when there is no matching cache entry (then the reload reads the arrays as the first load did).
